scope.summary: This standard specifies requirements for design, material, capacity, construction, and performance testing of steel drums with closed ends intended for packing and transporting bitumen with a penetration value of 225 and below.

certification_and_marking.certification_status: Strict Statutory Mandatory Certification. Under the 'Drums and Tins (Quality Control) Order' (QCO) issued by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry (DPIIT), Government of India, all bitumen drums must conform to IS 3575:1993 and bear the mandatory BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark). Enforcement dates transitioned for medium and large-scale enterprises on April 17, 2024, small enterprises on July 17, 2024, and micro enterprises on October 17, 2024. Manufacturing, importing, or selling non-certified bitumen drums is a punishable statutory offense under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable to industrial steel packaging.

requirements.detail: Every certified bitumen drum must bear the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) along with the manufacturer's registered licence number (CM/L) stenciled on the body or ends.
Drums are manufactured in two standard nominal capacities: 160 litres and 200 litres.
The drum shell must be fabricated from mild steel sheets or cold-rolled coils conforming to IS 513.
Drums must satisfy specified steel thickness requirements, typically utilizing 0.63 mm cold-rolled steel (24 SWG) to provide high durability and resist transport handling stress.
The longitudinal body seam must be continuously resistance welded to provide a completely airtight joint.
The fixed bottom and top ends must be securely attached to the shell using double-seamed joints along with a seaming compound resistant to hot bitumen.

Every finished drum must pass an air pressure leakage test before dispatch, holding an internal air pressure of 0.3 kg/cm² to 0.5 kg/cm² while submerged or sprayed with a soap solution, showing zero bubbles.
To guarantee seam security, sample drums filled with water to 98% capacity must withstand drop tests from specified heights onto solid concrete without leaking.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 3575 : 1993 is the mandatory national Indian Standard specification governing steel drums with fixed ends designed specifically for packing, storing, and transporting bulk bitumen and asphalt. Under India's statutory Drums and Tins Quality Control Order (QCO), all bitumen drums supplied or sold domestically must bear the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark). Crafted from high-quality cold-rolled steel sheets (conforming to IS 513) with a standard thickness of 0.63 mm (24 SWG), they are manufactured in 160-litre and 200-litre nominal capacities. The standard enforces strict quality and structural benchmarks—requiring continuously resistance-welded body seams, double-seamed ends, and 100% leak-proof security verified through high-impact drop tests and pneumatic air leakage testing.
